correctness.rationale: Writing \(A=2^a\), the pure two-power generating factor is \(H_A(z)=(1+z)(1-z^A)/(1-z)\), so its endpoint coefficients are one and all interior coefficients are two. The full degree enumerator factorizes as \(H_A(z)\prod_{j=1}^bH_A(z^{(p-1)p^{j-1}})\). Phi-practicality supplies at least one digit vector for each degree. If any digit is interior, its positive weight already contributes at least two. If every digit is an endpoint, complement symmetry reduces to a binary vector beginning with one; the explicit carry/replacement identities for \(p\le A-1\) or \(p=A+1\) produce another representation containing an interior digit. Hence every nontrivial coefficient is at least two. Degree one comes only from \(\Phi_1\) or \(\Phi_2\), so the exact minimum is two. Independent generating-function checks on several admissible families, including \((a,p,b)=(2,5,2)\) and \((4,17,1)\), reproduce the bound.

value.rationale: Phi-practicality is an existence property, and asking whether an interior degree has a unique cyclotomic-factor subset is the natural next multiplicity question. The theorem completely resolves that question for the full even two-prime-support family and identifies the exact minimum multiplicity, giving a structural strengthening rather than another membership test.
residual_risks: The result does not classify coefficient multiplicities for phi-practical integers with three or more distinct prime factors.
